newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Durch EVC slumps to year loss, sees PVC upturn.
newsitem.headline: Durch EVC slumps to year loss, sees PVC upturn.

text.p: Dutch plastics producer EVC on Wednesday blamed lower PVC prices and margins and pressure from a stronger lira and pound for its slump into a net 1996 loss.
Group net loss was 25 million guilders ($13.3 million) compared with 1995's profit of 163.9 million guilders, with turnover down by 18 percent to 2.09 billion guilders.
Europe's biggest polyvinyl chloride (PVC) maker, minority owned by ICI plc of Britain and Italy's Enichem, will, however, maintain the dividend at 3.00 guilders per share.
Operating profit dropped to 1.00 million guilders from 176.5 million guilders in 1995.

EVC said that turnover fell as a result of lower output of polymers, due largely to a 28 percent fall in the price of S-PVC, lower sale prices for compounds and declining sales of semi-manufactured and end-products.

The group had warned last August that it had fallen into small losses and did not expect much improvement, although it said on Wednesday that PVC markets had turned the corner and were expected to improve this year.

"In Western Europe the final quarter of 1996 already showed an improvement in (PVC) prices and volumes. This trend has continued into 1997, which gives reason for positive expectations this year, despite continued pressure on margins," EVC said in a statement.
It said the PVC industry was seen picking up worldwide as U.S. and Asian markets drove up prices and margins.
While extra production capacity was expected to come on line this would be largely offset by a rise in demand, it said.

"All in all these improvements, together with a continued contribution from the compounds, semi-manufactured and end-products division and a further optimisation of corporate units, is expected to lead to an improved result for EVC in 1997," the company said.
In early Amsterdam trading, EVC shares gained 2.60 guilders, or 4.8 percent, to 56.60 guilders each. ($ = 1.875 Dutch Guilders)
